targetWord.definition: a microorganism that can cause disease
exampleSentences: Bacteria and viruses are common pathogens.
The water was contaminated with dangerous pathogens.

clues.text: This word shares its root with "pathogenic" and "pathology".
Sometimes described as "virus", this noun describes a particular quality.
Often used in clinical or pathological discussions
For ten points, name this noun meaning "a microorganism that can cause disease".

tossups.text: This word shares its root with "pathogenic" and "pathology". Sometimes described as "virus", this noun describes a particular quality. Often used in clinical or pathological discussions For ten points, name this noun meaning "a microorganism that can cause disease".
tossups.explanation:
PATHOGEN (/ˈpæθədʒən/)

Definition: a microorganism that can cause disease

Etymology: From Greek pathos (disease) + genes (producing).

Example: "Bacteria and viruses are common pathogens."

Memory tip: PATHO-GEN = DISEASE (patho) PRODUCER (gen)

targetWord.definition: regularly found among particular people or in a certain area; native

etymology.narrative: From Greek endemos (native), from en- (in) + demos (people).

exampleSentences: Malaria is endemic to tropical regions.
Corruption has become endemic in that government.
targetWord.mnemonic: EN-demic = disease IN (en) the PEOPLE (demos) = always present there

targetWord.definition: characterized by reasoning from specific observations to broader generalizations

etymology.narrative: From Latin inductivus, from inducere (to lead in), from in- (into) + ducere (to lead).

exampleSentences: Inductive reasoning moves from specific cases to general principles.
Scientists use inductive methods to form hypotheses.

Definition: a medical specialist who treats disorders of the feet
